in_hebrew.name: צְפַנְיָה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: צְפַנְיָה, בֶּן מָכִיאָ, הוּא נַבִי הַיְהוּדִי, וְשֵׁם מָכִיאָ, הוּא, אֲבִיוֹ, הַנְּבִא. צְפַנְיָה, בָּנוֹ, נִקְרָא, בִּפְרוֹת, לְפָנָיו, וְנָבָא, וְהָיָה, נָבִיא, מִשְּׁלֹט, עַל, יְהוּדָה, וְעַל, גוֹי, הַגֹּויִים. צְפַנְיָה, הוּא, הַנְּבִא, אֲשֶׁר, נְבָא, בִּשְּׁנֵי, שֻׁלְעֲמִית, וּקְרִיעָת, יָמִים, וְאָמַר, לְאַרְבָּעִים, שָׁנָה, עַד, יוֹם, הַזֶּה, הַזֶּה, עָשָׂה, יְהוֹוָה, עִם, עַמּוֹ, וְאֵת, כָּל, מַלְכוּת, עַם, הַגֹּויִים, וְאֵת, כָּל, גֻּלְגְּלֶת, רַע, אֲשֶׁר, עָשָׂה, עִמָּם

in_greek.name: Ζεφανιὰς
in_greek.long_meaning: Ζεφανιὰς, ὁ υἱός του Μακίγια, ἦν προφήτης Ἰουδαῖος. Ὁ Μακίγια, ὁ πατήρ του Ζεφανιὰ, ἦταν ἱερεύς. Ὁ Ζεφανιὰς ὁ υἱός του, προφήτης ἦταν, καὶ ὑπῆρξε προφήτης, τῆς Ιουδαίας, καὶ τοῦ λαοῦ τοῦ δυνάμενοι. Ο Ζεφανιὰς ὁ προφήτης ἦταν ὁ ὁποῖος ἐλάλησε, εἰς ἐτέστι τὰς δύο, τῶν ἱερέων, καὶ τὴν κρίσιν, τῶν καιρῶν. Ὁ Ζεφανιὰς ὁ προφήτης ἐλάλησε, εἰς ἑπτὰ ἑβδομάδες, καὶ εἶπε, ὅτι, ὁ Κύριος, ἐποίησε, σὺν τῷ λαῷ, αὐτοῦ, καὶ εἶπε, ὅτι, αὐτὸς ἐποίησε, τὴν ἐξουσίαν, τῶν βασιλέων, τοῦ λαοῦ τοῦ δυνάμενοι, καὶ ἔλεγε, ὅτι, πᾶσαν τὴν κακίαν, ἣν ἐποίησαν, ἐν τῷ λαῷ, αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐν τῷ λαῷ, τοῦ δυνάμενοι

in_latin.name: Zephaniah
in_latin.long_meaning: Zephaniah filius Machias propheta Iudaicus. Machias pater Zephaniae sacerdos erat. Zephaniae filii propheta erat, et propheta factus est, super Iudam, et super gentem gentium. Zephaniae propheta, qui prophetaverit in septem hebdomadibus, et dixit, quod Dominus fecit cum populo suo, et dixit, quod ipse fecit potestatem regum populi gentium, et dixit, quod omni malitia quae fecerunt in populo suo, et in populo gentium

in_english.name: Zephaniah
in_english.long_meaning: Zephaniah, son of Cushi, was a prophet of Judah. Cushi was the father of Zephaniah, who was a priest. Zephaniah the prophet was a prophet who prophesied in the days of Josiah, the king of Judah. Zephaniah prophesied that God would cut off the nations that were oppressing Judah, and that He would judge the people of Judah for their sins. The name Zephaniah is derived from the Hebrew words 'zephani' meaning 'hidden' or 'protected', and 'yah' meaning 'God' or 'Jehovah'. It is also related to the word 'safan', which means 'watchman' or 'guardian'. In Christian tradition, the name Zephaniah is associated with the virtues of watchfulness, protection, and guardianship. It is also associated with the themes of justice, righteousness, and the judgment of God.

data.cultural_impact: The name Zephaniah is of Hebrew origin, which means 'God has remembered the south'. data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Zephaniah is rooted in its meaning 'God of the South Wind'. The name evokes a sense of divine presence and intervention, as if God is reaching out to His people with a breath of fresh wind. It also speaks of God's faithfulness and remembrance, as the people of Judah were not forgetten by God despite their waywardness. The name Zephaniah serves as a reminder that God is always with us, always watching, always caring, and always ready to remember us and guide us through even the toughest times.

He is best known for his oracles against the nations, particularly against the Philistines and the Ethiopians.
